## Intent
Hypothesis: Halide code generation for the math-expressible integration loop can match compiler auto-vectorization while maintaining bit-exactness, without intermediate storage.

## Layout & approach
The AoS layout at 68 B/particle offers poor locality: loop1 touches 24/68 B (35% hot), loop2 8/68 (11%), loop3 28/68 (41%) — the rest is dead weight. With no intermediate storage the death verdict stays in registers, but each loop re-walks the full 68-byte stride. The working set spills L1d at N≈481 and L2 at N≈7710, so all measured points (N≥10000) are L3-resident or DRAM. Each 68-byte particle spans two 64B lines, wasting 59–89% of fetched bandwidth per loop.

## Cache saturation
All measured N are L3-resident (10000, 100000) or DRAM (1000000, 10000000); L1→L2 and L2→L3 transitions are not resolved by the grid. The L3→DRAM transition at N≈246723 produces a modest rise: at q=0.01, 25.6→30.0 ns/p (+17%); at q=0.5, 34.3→37.4 (+9%). Within each regime cost is flat (25.7 vs 25.6 at q=0.01 L3; 30.0 vs 29.1 at q=0.01 DRAM), confirming the bottleneck is per-particle overhead, not cache capacity.

## Bandwidth
The memory floor is 5.359 ns/p; the algo's best (25.6) is 4.8x above it, worst (37.4) is 7.0x. Achieved bandwidth peaks at 2.65 GB/s (21% of the 12.69 ceiling), falling to 1.82 GB/s (14%) at q=0.5 DRAM. The algo is frontend-bound: 62–72% frontend stalls mean the core cannot saturate memory. Ratios vs baseline are near unity (0.99–1.13x) everywhere — Halide loop1 yields no advantage because loop2 and loop3 dominate and are scalar. The winner gap narrows with death rate: 3.34x slower at q=0.01 but 1.97x at q=0.5.

## Assembly
Codegen is entirely scalar — zero vector-suffixed instructions. Loop1 is a `call` to `halide_b5_math`. Loop2 uses `vmovss`/`vucomiss` for the death check, branchy `jae` to `call Data.spawn`; inline RNG uses `xor`, `rorx`, `shl`, `lzcnt`. Loop3 does byte-granular scatter: `movzx` loads, `add`, `cmp`/`cmovae` clamping, then `mov BYTE PTR` stores — three byte stores per pixel. The 440-instruction footprint and branching (27 `cmp`, 11 `jae`, 12 `cmovae`) explain the 62–72% frontend stalls. Scalar `vmovss`/`vmulss`/`vaddss` process one float at a time; the byte scatter prevents streaming benefit.

## Verdict
Refuted — 0.99–1.13x of naive baseline at every point, and 1.97–3.34x slower than the winner (AF02.LP1-autovec.LP2-opt). The Halide loop1 call is dwarfed by scalar, branchy loop2 (RNG + spawn) and loop3 (byte-granular scatter), which produce 62–72% frontend stalls and zero vectorization, capping bandwidth at 14–21% of ceiling. No-intermediate-storage keeps the verdict in registers but cannot compensate for the AoS layout's 59–89% dead-byte fraction and entirely scalar codegen.
